title: Australia defeats Bangladesh in two days to tie cricket series
seoTitle: Australia beats Bangladesh in two days to tie series
subtitle: Led by a stellar performance from Mitchell Starc, the Australian team won the second Test by an innings and 51 runs
excerpt: Australia overcame Bangladesh in the second Test cricket match. The victory by an innings and 51 runs secured a series tie after just two days of play.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The Australian national team secured a victory over Bangladesh in the second Test cricket match, ensuring a tie in the series between the two sides. The clash was wrapped up in just two days following an Australian comeback, as they won the match by an innings and 51 runs.

Mitchell Starc's Performance

One of the standout names of the match was player Mitchell Starc. He delivered a decisive performance by taking a total of 10 wickets throughout the game, directly helping Australia overcome their opponents and swiftly seal a favorable result.

How the Test Format Works in Cricket

To grasp the dynamics of this result, it is important to understand the general rules of the sport. The Test format is the most traditional and longest form of cricket. Originally, these matches are scheduled to last up to five days, with teams taking turns attacking and defending, known as innings.

When a team wins by "an innings and runs," it means they accumulated such a high score in their first batting turn that the opponent, even after combining both of their batting chances, failed to surpass that total. Consequently, there is no need for the winning team to take their second turn at bat, bringing the game to an early end.

The Role of Wickets and the Series Tie

In cricket, the term "wicket" refers to the dismissal of an opposing batter by the fielding team. A bowler who manages to take 10 dismissals in a single match achieves a significant milestone for their team's strategy. With the dismissal of the Bangladeshi batters, Australia managed to close out the match in just two days.

International Test series generally consist of a set of matches to determine an overall winner. With Australia's victory in this second encounter, following the team's rebound, the series against Bangladesh officially ended in a draw.
